```{r, setup, include=FALSE}
library(eStar)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
library(viridis)
library(kableExtra)

colors <- viridis(n = 5, option = "plasma")
names(colors) <- c("Metric", "Baseline", "Disturbed", "LRR", "Difference")
resp_colscale <- scale_colour_manual(values = colors)
```

# Toy data set
```{r toy-data, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 7, fig.cap = "Figure 1: Time-series of the state variable created for the toy data set. Values in a 'disturbed' system (dark pink) show a steep decrease at time step 10, while the baseline (purlple) does not. Also represented are values often derived to calculate the stability metrics: long response ratio between the values in disturbed and in the baseline time-series (orange) and the difference between them (yellow)."}
sv_df <- dplyr::left_join(dplyr::rename(toy_blts, "svbl" = stat_var),
          dplyr::rename(toy_dbts, "svdb" = stat_var),
          by = "time") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(lrr = log(svdb/svbl),
                  diff = svdb - svbl) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c("svbl", "svdb", "lrr", "diff"),
                        names_to = "response", values_to = "value")%>%
    dplyr::mutate(data = dplyr::recode_factor(response,
                                              "svdb" = "Disturbed",
                                              "svbl" = "Baseline",
                                              "lrr" = "LRR",
                                              "diff" = "Difference"))

(sv_plot <- sv_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = time, y = value, colour = data, group = data)) +
    geom_line(size = 0.8)+
    geom_point(size = 0.8)+
    resp_colscale+
    labs(x = "Time", y = "Response measure", color = "Data")+
    theme_minimal()+
    theme(legend.position = c(0.80, 0.20),
          legend.background = element_rect(fill =  "white", colour = "white")))
```

Description of values generated for the disturbed system:
```{r}
?toy_dbts
```

Description of values generated for the baseline system:
```{r}
?toy_blts
```

```{r eval=FALSE, include = FALSE}
toy_blts, toy_svts %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = "Example formatting of input time-series of a) disturbed system and b) baseline.") %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))
```

# Main functions
Examples of each function applied to the toy dataset.

TODO: add descriptions of arguments

## Invariability

Invariability calculated as the inverse of standard deviation of residuals of the 
linear model fitted to predict the log response ratio from time, over a defined 
time frame (`metric_df`, Fig. 2-a).
```{r}
invariability(
    svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", response = "lrr", mode = "lm_res",
    metric_tf = c(11, 50), db_data = toy_dbts, svbl_i = "stat_var",
    tbl_i = "time", bl_data = toy_blts
)
```

Invariability calculated as the inverse of standard deviation of residuals of the
linear model fitted to predict the state variable from time (Fig. 2-b).
```{r}
invariability(
    svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", response = "sv", mode = "lm_res",
    metric_tf = c(11, 50), db_data = toy_dbts, svbl_i = "stat_var",
    tbl_i = "time", bl_data = toy_blts
)
```

Invariability calculated as the inverse of the coefficient of variation of the log
response ratio (Fig. 2-c).
```{r}
invariability(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", response = "lrr", mode = "cv",
   metric_tf = c(11, 50), db_data = toy_dbts, svbl_i = "stat_var",
    tbl_i = "time", bl_data = toy_blts
)
```

Invariability calculated as the inverse of the coefficient of variation of a state 
variable (Fig. 2-d).
```{r}
invariability(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", response = "sv", mode = "cv",
   metric_tf = c(11, 50), db_data = toy_dbts
)
```

```{r invar_schem, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Figure 2: Schematic representation of the possible metrics of invariability available in the eStar package. 'LRR' refers to the log response ratio between the disturbed and baseline time-series, and 'SV', to 'state variable'", out.width = '100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("/home/luf74xx/Dokumente/postdoc/eStar_main/eStar/vignettes/invariability.png")
```
## Resistance

Resistance calculated in relation to a baseline time series (`bl = "input"`), 
as the log response ratio (`res_mode = "lrr"`) at the first time step following 
disturbance (`res_time = "defined"`, `res_t = 11`, Fig. 3-e,f).
```{r}
resistance(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, bl = "input",
   svbl_i = "stat_var", tbl_i = "time", bl_data = toy_blts,
   res_mode = "lrr", res_time = "defined", res_t = 11
)
```

Resistance calculated in relation to a baseline time series (`bl = "input"`), 
as the highest (`res_mode = "max"`) log response ratio (`res_mode = "lrr"`) 
during a given time frame (`res_tf = c(11, 50)`, Fig. 3-g,h).
```{r}
resistance(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, bl = "input",
   svbl_i = "stat_var", tbl_i = "time", bl_data = toy_blts,
   res_mode = "lrr", res_time = "max", res_tf = c(11, 50)
)
```

Resistance calculated in relation to a baseline time series (`bl = "input"`), 
as the difference (`res_mode = "diff"`) at the first time step following 
disturbance (`res_time = "defined"`, `res_t = 11`, Fig. 3-i,j).
```{r}
resistance(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, bl = "input",
   svbl_i = "stat_var", tbl_i = "time", bl_data = toy_blts,
   res_mode = "diff", res_time = "defined", res_t = 11
)
```

Resistance calculated in relation to a baseline time series (`bl = "input"`), 
as the highest (`res_mode = "max"`) absolute difference (`res_mode = "diff"`) 
during a given time frame (`res_tf = c(11, 50)`, Fig. 3-k,l).
```{r}
resistance(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, bl = "input",
   svbl_i = "stat_var", tbl_i = "time", bl_data = toy_blts,
   res_mode = "diff", res_time = "max", res_tf = c(11, 50)
)
```

```{r resistance_schem, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Figure 3: Schematic representation of the possible metrics of resistance available in the eStar package. 'LRR' refers to the log response ratio between the disturbed and baseline time-series, 'SV', to 'state variable', 'td+1', to the first time step after disturbance, and 'tlow', to the time step of highest response in relation to the baseline.", out.width = '100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("/home/luf74xx/Dokumente/postdoc/eStar_main/eStar/vignettes/resistance.png")
```
## Extent of recovery
Extent of recovery as the log response ratio in relation to a baseline value
(`bl = "input"`), at time step (`t_rec = 50`, Fig. 4-m,n).
```{r eval=FALSE}
recovery_extent(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, response = "lrr",
   bl = "input", t_rec = 50, svbl_i = "stat_var", tbl_i = "time",
   bl_data = toy_blts
) 
```
Extent of recovery as the difference in relation to a baseline value
(`bl = "input"`), at time step (`t_rec = 50`, Fig. 4-o,p).
```{r eval=FALSE}
recovery_extent(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, response = "lrr",
   bl = "input", t_rec = 50, svbl_i = "stat_var", tbl_i = "time",
   bl_data = toy_blts
)
```
Extent of recovery as the log response ratio in relation to a pre-disturbance 
(`bl = "db"`) mean value (`summ_mode = "mean"` by default, summarized over 
`bl_tf = c(5, 10)`), at time step (`t_rec = 50`).
```{r eval=FALSE}
recovery_extent(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, response = "lrr",
   bl = "db", t_rec = 50, bl_tf = c(5, 10)
)
```
```{r echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Figure 4: Schematic representation of the possible metrics of extent of recovery available in the eStar package. 'LRR' refers to the log response ratio between the disturbed and baseline time-series, 'Diff', to the difference between them, and 'tpost', to a post-disturbance time step.", out.width = '100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("/home/luf74xx/Dokumente/postdoc/eStar_main/eStar/vignettes/extent_recovery.png")
```

## Rate of recovery

Rate of recovery calculated as the slope of the linear model which predicts the 
log response ratio in relation to a baseline (`bl = "input`) is predicted by 
time (over a time frame (`metric_tf = c(12, 50)`, Fig. 5-q).
```{r}
recovery_rate(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, bl = "input",
   metric_tf = c(12, 50), svbl_i = "stat_var", tbl_i = "time", bl_data = toy_blts
)
```

Rate of recovery calculated as the slope of the linear model which predicts the 
the values of the state variable  (`bl = "db`) is predicted by time (over a time
frame (`metric_tf = c(12, 50)`, Fig. 5-r).
```{r}
recovery_rate(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, bl = "db",
   metric_tf = c(12, 50), svbl_i = "stat_var", tbl_i = "time", bl_data = toy_blts
)
```

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Figure 5: Schematic representation of the possible metrics of rate of recovery available in the eStar package. 'LRR' refers to the log response ratio between the disturbed and baseline time-series, 'SV', to 'state variable'. The blue solid line identifies the linear model fitted to predict the response from time (along with its equation) and the double-headed arrow identifies the slope, which is the measure of rate of recovery", out.width = '100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("/home/luf74xx/Dokumente/postdoc/eStar_main/eStar/vignettes/rate_recovery.png")
```

## Persistence

Limits of persistence defined by the state variable values in an independent 
baseline (`bl = "input"`) during the same post-disturbance time period 
for which persistence is measured (`metric_tf = c(50, 100)`, Fig. 6).
```{r}
persistence(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, bl = "input",
   metric_tf = c(50, 100), svbl_i = "stat_var", tbl_i = "time",
   bl_data = toy_blts
)
```

Limits of persistence defined by the state variable values during a pre-disturbance
(`bl = "db"`) time period (`bl_tf = c(1, 9)`). Persistence is measured for the 
post-disturbance time period (`metric_tf = c(50, 100)`, Fig. 6).
```{r}
persistence(
   svdb_i = "stat_var", tdb_i = "time", db_data = toy_dbts, bl = "db",
   bl_tf = c(1, 9), metric_tf = c(50, 100)
)
```

```{r fig.cap="Figure 6: Schematic representation of the possible metrics of persistence available in the eStar package. 'SV' refers to 'state variable', 'limu' and 'liml' are the upper and lower limits characterizing persistence, 'ta' is the period for which persistence is calculated for, and 'tP', the period during which the state variable remained inside the limits.", out.width = '100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("/home/luf74xx/Dokumente/postdoc/eStar_main/eStar/vignettes/persistence.png")
```
